title: C4466 — Right exhaust valve solenoid connector
introduction:
I read this reference like a plug's address book: the connector identity tells me which entry to open, the drawing locates its cavity labels, and the circuit table explains what each address serves. Start with the component description, then match the harness heading before reading across a cavity's row.

This is a connector-reading guide. It supplies neither physical access instructions nor an electrical test. The drawing's physical viewing direction, the gauge convention and the meanings of Size and Used are unspecified here; keep those entries as recorded rather than turning them into probing or wire-selection instructions.

edits.why: In the drawing, the cavity labels run vertically inside the elongated face, beside the larger rectangular housing detail on the left. I use those visible shapes to navigate the illustration, without assuming that its page orientation establishes how to view an installed connector. The table beneath ties the illustrated face to its harness and shell entry.

Read from Cavity across to Circuit Number, Color, Gauge and Function. The functions distinguish the powertrain-controller connection, the fuse-or-circuit-breaker connection and the body-ground connection. Because the recorded colors are identical, color alone cannot distinguish the rows. Matching a row identifies its documented circuit role; it does not prove that the circuit or solenoid works.

The service-part field identifies the cataloged pigtail entry, while Engineering Shell identifies its associated housing. I keep those identities separate: the housing's name is not automatically the ordering number for the complete pigtail. Use this table as a parts reference alongside the applicable repair information; it supplies no splice, terminal-release or replacement sequence.
